stem: A telephone-triage nurse receives a caller reporting new chest pressure and shortness of breath. Which action best reflects the RN's role?

options.A: Diagnose acute coronary syndrome from the telephone history and give the caller a definitive cardiac diagnosis.
options.B: Perform a focused assessment, recognize a possible emergency, and direct activation of emergency medical services according to protocol and scope.
options.C: Complete a detailed lifetime health history before deciding whether emergency evaluation is needed.
options.D: Recommend a prescription medication for the chest pressure without an authorized order, protocol, or prescriber involvement.

rationale: NHLBI identifies chest pressure or discomfort and shortness of breath among heart-attack warning symptoms and advises calling 9-1-1 for emergency medical care even when the person is not certain that a heart attack is occurring. The 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan requires prioritization based on acuity, use of referrals/resources, and practice within legal scope. Therefore B is the best nursing action: obtain a focused assessment sufficient to recognize the possible emergency and direct EMS activation according to the applicable protocol and scope. A exceeds the available information by making a definitive remote diagnosis, C delays time-sensitive care, and D recommends prescription treatment without an authorized mechanism.
educational_objective: In telephone triage, recognize new chest pressure with shortness of breath as a possible emergency, prioritize EMS evaluation, and act within authorized nursing protocols rather than making a definitive remote diagnosis or independently prescribing treatment.
source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN); National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NHLBI), NIH
source_document_title: 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; Heart Attack — Symptoms and Diagnosis
source_version_date: NCSBN Test Plan effective April 1, 2026 through March 31, 2029; NHLBI heart-attack guidance currentness rechecked August 16, 2026
source_locator: NCSBN Management of Care, printed pp.21-22: Establishing Priorities — prioritize delivery of client care based on acuity; Legal Rights and Responsibilities — recognize limitations/use resources and provide care within legal scope; Referrals — assess need for referral. NHLBI Heart Attack > Symptoms: chest discomfort/pressure and shortness of breath are warning symptoms; When to call 9-1-1: call for emergency medical care even if unsure. Heart Attack > Diagnosis: call 9-1-1/get to the emergency room quickly when heart attack is suspected.
source_claim_supported: New chest pressure with shortness of breath can represent a time-sensitive cardiac emergency requiring EMS evaluation; the RN should prioritize acuity and referral within scope rather than provide a definitive telephone diagnosis or unauthorized prescription treatment.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Management of Care, printed pp.21-22: Establishing Priorities — prioritize delivery of client care based on acuity; Legal Rights and Responsibilities — recognize limitations of self and others and utilize resources; provide care within legal scope of practice; Referrals — assess need for referral and obtain necessary orders.
blueprint_topic: Management of Care — telephone triage prioritization, referral, resources, and scope

source_original.stem: A telephone-triage nurse receives a caller reporting new chest pressure and shortness of breath. Which action best reflects the RN's role?

options.A: Diagnose acute coronary syndrome from the telephone history and provide a definitive diagnosis to the caller.
options.B: Perform a focused assessment, recognize a possible emergency, and direct urgent evaluation according to protocol and scope.
options.C: Complete a detailed lifetime history before deciding whether emergency evaluation is needed.
options.D: Recommend a prescription drug for chest pain without an authorized order, protocol, or prescriber involvement.

source_original.rationale: Telephone triage requires nursing assessment and clinical judgment within scope, not remote definitive diagnosis or unauthorized prescribing. New chest pressure with dyspnea can represent an emergency, so Option B appropriately prioritizes urgent evaluation. A exceeds the information available, C delays care, and D exceeds scope absent an authorized mechanism.
source_original.source_detail: Management of Care activity statements: establish priorities for care, facilitate referrals and follow-up, collaborate with the interprofessional team, use resources, and provide care within legal scope; clinical judgment is integrated throughout the plan. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness live-rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care: prioritization, assignment/delegation, advocacy/client rights, continuity/referral, legal scope, professional limitations and emergency/quality-management activities as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

correction_summary: Retained the telephone-triage construct and key B. Replaced vague 'urgent evaluation' wording with the directly supported EMS/9-1-1 response for a chest-pressure/shortness-of-breath warning pattern, while retaining protocol/scope language. Added NHLBI/NIH as the clinical source for emergency urgency and used NCSBN for prioritization, referral, and scope. No definitive diagnosis or medication protocol was invented.

audit_findings.clinical_category: Telephone triage of possible acute cardiac emergency
audit_findings.source_authority: Official NCSBN 2026 Test Plan for prioritization/scope; NHLBI/NIH for heart-attack warning symptoms and EMS urgency
audit_findings.currentness: NCSBN current 2026-2029 Test Plan; NHLBI pages live-rechecked 2026-08-16
audit_findings.exact_locator: NCSBN Management of Care > Establishing Priorities, Legal Rights and Responsibilities, Referrals; NHLBI Heart Attack > Symptoms > When to call 9-1-1 and Heart Attack > Diagnosis
audit_findings.claim_audit: The final item makes no remote ACS diagnosis. It uses directly supported symptom urgency and requires focused nursing assessment, EMS referral, and protocol/scope adherence. No medication dose, treatment timing threshold, or telephone-prescribing authority is invented.

distractor_audit.A: Incorrect because the RN cannot establish a definitive acute coronary syndrome diagnosis from this limited telephone history.
distractor_audit.B: Correct: recognizes acuity and directs EMS evaluation while remaining within protocol/scope.
distractor_audit.C: Incorrect because a lifetime history delays emergency disposition for a time-sensitive warning pattern.
distractor_audit.D: Incorrect because it recommends prescription treatment without an authorized order/protocol/prescriber mechanism.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only B combines emergency recognition, appropriate referral, and scope-limited nursing action; no second option is defensible.
audit_findings.cueing: All alternatives describe plausible telephone-triage actions; the correct answer is not identified by a numeric threshold or unique diagnosis label.
audit_findings.blueprint: Management of Care — Establishing Priorities, Referrals, and Legal Scope of Practice.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Re-audited the NHLBI emergency recommendation, NCSBN PDF text and rendered Management of Care pages, stem, all alternatives, rationale, objective, scope language, ambiguity, cueing, and unsupported precision. B remained uniquely best.
